test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In relation to fiscal deficit, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Fiscal deficit = Primary deficit - Interest payments
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings
Greater fiscal deficit implies lesser borrowing by the government
Fiscal deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts

solution:
The correct answer is **Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts excluding borrowings:**

 
 
• This formula accurately defines the fiscal deficit. It represents the gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding any borrowings).
 
• The fiscal deficit indicates how much the government needs to borrow to meet its expenditure requirements.
 
• A higher fiscal deficit implies greater borrowing needs, influencing the overall economic stability and interest rates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal deficit = Primary deficit - Interest payments:**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. The primary deficit is calculated as the fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore, the fiscal deficit includes the primary deficit and interest payments, not the other way around.
 
 
 
• **Greater fiscal deficit implies lesser borrowing by the government:**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect. A greater fiscal deficit actually implies greater borrowing needs by the government to cover the shortfall between its expenditure and revenue.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts:**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect. While it partially captures the concept, it misses out on capital expenditure and receipts which are also part of the total expenditure and total receipts, respectively.
